newsitem.title: USA: Ivory cocoa arrivals seen at 625,000 T to Jan 11.
newsitem.headline: Ivory cocoa arrivals seen at 625,000 T to Jan 11.

text.p: Total cumulative Ivory Coast arrivals were "guesstimated" at some 625,000 tonnes through January 11, compared with an estimated 740,000 tonnes at the same time last year, trade house General Cocoa said in a weekly newsletter.

Other market sources put total cumulative arrivals at about 650,000 tonnes, the newsletter said, but the discrepancy appears to stem from a difference in the starting date from which the arrivals were calculated.

"The 625,000-tonne figure is believed to be the total since the offical opening of the 1996/97 season, October 14," General Cocoa said, "while the 650,000-tonne estimate apparently represents the total from October 1."

The report said estimates for the Ivorian main crop remained at some 900,000 tonnes, but that the preliminary forecast for the 1997 mid crop was "somewhat pessimistic" due to dry weather in the cocoa growing regions.
"While it is much too early for any reliable estimates, initial trade forecasts range from 110,000 to 150,000 metric tons," it said.

Total 1996/97 Ivorian cocoa sales were estimated at around 860,000 tonnes, including a "guesstimated" portion of price-fixation completed against the long-term cocoabean contract with a leading trade house and price-fixed cocoa products contracts.
General Cocoa said total Ivorian 1997/98 sales were estiamted at some 185,000 tonnes, including price-fixation against cocoabean and cocoa products contracts to date.
